title: Chapter 10
paragraphs: From that time a new life began for Alexey Alexandrovitch and his wife. Nothing in particular happened. Anna went out into society as she had always done, was especially often at Princess Betsy's, and met Vronsky everywhere. Alexey Alexandrovitch saw this, but could do nothing about it. All his efforts to draw her into open discussion she met with a barrier he could not penetrate, made up of a kind of amused perplexity. Outwardly everything was the same, but their inner relations had completely changed. Alexey Alexandrovitch, a man of great power in the world of politics, felt himself helpless in this. Like an ox with its head bent, he submissively awaited the blow that he sensed was raised over him. Every time he began to think about it, he felt he must try once more, that by kindness, tenderness, and persuasion there was still hope of saving her, of bringing her back to herself, and every day he prepared to talk to her. But every time he began to talk to her, he felt that the spirit of evil and deception that had taken possession of her had possession of him too, and he spoke to her in a tone quite unlike that in which he had meant to speak. In spite of himself he addressed her in his habitual tone of jeering at anyone who would say what he was saying. And in that tone it was impossible to say what needed to be said to her.
